title: Marigold Financial vendor onboarding — DPA / SLA / KMS preflight
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-28 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Evan Morales (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Sofia Alvarez (Marigold - Procurement); Ravi Patel (Marigold - Security); Maya Chen (Marigold - Legal)
summary: Alignment call to run through Marigold's legal and procurement checklists. Focus areas: DPA redlines, SLA thresholds for latency/uptime, key management options (KMS/HSM), egress and billing model concerns, and a short pilot scope. Agreed to share security whitepaper and a billing comparison spreadsheet; follow-up pilot to validate latency on dedicated vs hosted with sample workload.
topics: KMS options and keying model (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)
action_items: Evan Morales: share DPA redline rationales + sample MSA clause mapping (due 2026-10-05)
Priya Shah: prepare pilot runbook and sample workload to validate 99th pct latency across dedicated/hosted (due 2026-10-07)
Ravi Patel: provide Marigold's minimum crypto requirements and KMS audit checklist (due 2026-10-04)
Maya Chen: circulate internal procurement timeline and any mandatory contract clauses we need to confirm (due 2026-10-06)
next_steps: Redwood to upload security whitepaper and KMS integration doc to shared drive by EOD 2026-09-29
Schedule pilot kickoff (1hr) week of 2026-10-11 once Marigold shares sample traffic
Legal teams to review DPA redlines and reconvene if there are >3 substantive redlines
transcript:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're short on time but wanted to run through procurement and security asks.
[00:12] Sofia (Marigold): Hi hi, thanks. Quick agenda from our side is DPA items, SLA numbers, and KMS. We also have a couple of billing questions.
[00:27] Priya (Redwood): Great, we'll start with the DPA — Evan do you want to take the redlines?
[00:32] Evan (Redwood): Sure. So, high level Redwood's standard DPA covers processor obligations, subprocessor list, data retention and deletion, and incident response. We marked the three clauses you flagged — section 4, 7, and appendix B — with notes. I'll share the rationale.
[01:05] Maya (Marigold): On appendix B, our counsel is concerned about the indemnity bucket. They want clearer limits when data is misused by a subprocessor.
[01:18] Evan (Redwood): Totally. Our legal can either accept tighter language or propose escrowed liability cap language. We try to avoid open-ended indemnity but we can propose a compromise.
[01:30] Ravi (Marigold): Real quick, on-data residency — we need to confirm logs and traces do not cross EU boundaries for EU customers.
[01:42] Priya (Redwood): For hosted deployments we have region controls and logging retention can be regionalized. For Dedicated/Private, you run in your VPC and we don't have access to data plane logs, only control plane telemetry that is obfuscated.
[02:05] Sofia (Marigold): That sounds fine, but procurement will need proof. Do you have SOC reports or an ISO cert?
[02:14] Evan (Redwood): Yes, SOC2 Type II in our security pack; we'll attach that along with the security whitepaper.
[02:24] Maya (Marigold): Perfect.
[02:31] Evan (Redwood): Moving to SLAs — what are the must-haves for you? Is it strictly uptime percentages, or do you need tail-latency SLOs?
[02:41] Sofia (Marigold): Uptime is table stakes. But product team is sensitive to 99th percentile latency for synchronous features. If a model call hits 2s for 99th that triggers bad UX.
[02:56] Priya (Redwood): Right, our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% regional availability. For 99th percentile latency we provide per-route dashboards; we can include commitments for dedicated pools, and also a fallback policy — if latency exceeds a threshold we can route to a cached/quantized variant.
[03:18] Ravi (Marigold): When you say 'quantized variant' — is that another model with lower accuracy? We can't degrade customer-facing recommendations too much.
[03:27] Priya (Redwood): It's model variant dependent, but we can pin quality tests and have automatic rollback if quality degrades beyond agreed-upon eval metrics. We'll include sample eval thresholds in the pilot runbook.
[03:42] Sofia (Marigold): And pricing — our cost team is worried about egress and token-based billing spikes. Do you expose per-token unit economics?
[03:52] Evan (Redwood): Yes, we provide token-level breakdowns and can produce an estimated cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated. Egress is charged per GB for some enterprise plans; dedicated pools have different billing assumptions in the reserved contract.
[04:07] Maya (Marigold): Can you send an example bill with sample traffic? Procurement wants an apples-to-apples for our analysis.
[04:14] Evan (Redwood): We'll do that — a billing comparison sheet with modeled traffic.
[04:20] [05:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible) ... apologies, noise at my end
[05:12] Priya (Redwood): Back to KMS — Marigold mentioned customer-managed keys. We support both provider-managed and customer-managed keying. Customer KMS integration works via an HSM-backed KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSM with PKCS#11).
[05:39] Ravi (Marigold): We need CMK (customer-managed keys) and per-tenant key isolation. Also rotation windows of 90 days and audit trails for key usage.
[05:51] Priya (Redwood): Understood. For Dedicated/Private deploys we offer key injection so keys never transit Redwood control plane. For hosted we still can support CMEK via envelope encryption; keys stay in customer's KMS and we only store wrapped keys.
[06:10] Maya (Marigold): Is there an additional fee for customer-managed keys?
[06:16] Evan (Redwood): There's typically an operational fee depending on the KMS connector and HSM usage; we'll include the KMS pricing line-item in the bill model.
[06:26] Sofia (Marigold): Also, procurement flagged the need for audit logs proving who accessed the model and the prompts for certain regulated workflows. How granular are your logs?
[06:36] Priya (Redwood): We emit request-level telemetry, but PII is redacted by default. You can configure logging retention and fields. For private deployments we can enable detailed access logs that are retained in your S3 or log destination per your retention policy.
[06:52] Ravi (Marigold): Good. We also want a flow for emergency key revocation — if a key is compromised we need a documented playbook.
[07:02] Priya (Redwood): We'll include an emergency key revocation playbook in the security doc set. It covers rotation, rewrap, and canary rollout steps.
[07:12] Evan (Redwood): Quick note on egress: compressed KV-cache and prefix caching reduce traffic for repeated prompts; that often cuts egress and token usage. We'll model that in the pilot.
[07:28] Sofia (Marigold): Pilot scope — we want a two-week pilot, sample traffic of about 100k inference requests/day, mixture of short chat queries and longer context calls. Can you replicate that on a dedicated pool sandbox?
[07:44] Priya (Redwood): Yes — we can provision a dedicated sandbox with autoscaling limits to mirror production. We'll capture 95/99 pct latencies and cost breakdown.
[07:55] Maya (Marigold): Will the pilot require production data or anonymized?
[07:59] Priya (Redwood): For initial tests anonymized data is fine; if you need to run with real PII we recommend Private deployment or strict data handling agreements.
[08:12] Evan (Redwood): On contract timing — what's your procurement runway?
[08:16] Sofia (Marigold): Targeting vendor selection by end of October, internal signoff mid-November.
[08:23] Evan (Redwood): Makes sense — we'll aim to have a pilot report before the selection date.
[08:30] [10:00] Ravi (Marigold): A couple of technical points — are there export controls on model weights? We need to ensure no restricted data leaves certain enclaves.
[10:10] Priya (Redwood): We maintain model provenance and can restrict model variants by region. For private/on-prem we can guarantee models stay inside the enclave; for hosted we can apply region routing policies.
[10:22] Sofia (Marigold): Also, about termination and data deletion — procurement wants to ensure data wipe within X days on contract termination and certificate of deletion.
[10:33] Evan (Redwood): Standard is 30 days for hosted unless otherwise requested; we can push to 14 for enterprise contracts. We'll add a certificate of deletion process.
[10:45] Maya (Marigold): On indemnity, can you confirm cyber-liability limits and whether you carry breach insurance?
[10:53] Evan (Redwood): We carry breach insurance and can provide a copy of the insurance certificate; liability caps can be discussed in the MSA edits.
[11:02] Sofia (Marigold): Good.
[11:08] Priya (Redwood): Quick demo note — we'll avoid a full product demo in this call, but Priya will run a lightweight smoke test during the pilot and share dashboards.
[11:18] Evan (Redwood): For the DPA redlines — Maya, can you call out the top three that would block procurement?
[11:24] Maya (Marigold): Yes: 1) Indemnity/limits of liability, 2) Data residency and cross-border logs, 3) Subprocessor visibility and right-to-audit.
[11:36] Evan (Redwood): Great, we'll propose language around capped indemnity and more detailed subprocessor disclosures.
[11:44] [15:00] Speaker 2: (some background)
[15:10] Priya (Redwood): On the technical side we should also define success metrics: 99th pctl latency < 1.2s for short chat, availability 99.9, and error rate < 0.1% over a rolling 24h. We can instrument those in the pilot.
[15:31] Ravi (Marigold): The product team wants to ensure model hallucination rate is monitored; any automated tooling to detect regressions?
[15:40] Priya (Redwood): Yes we can run evals tied to prompt suites and set regression alerts. We'll attach a sample prompt set.
[15:48] Sofia (Marigold): Can you also show us how rollouts work — can we do canary with traffic split?
[15:55] Priya (Redwood): Canary and A/B are supported; routing policy can be performance-based or manual. Canary rules and rollback windows are configurable.
[16:06] Evan (Redwood): We're going to share three documents: DPA commentary, security whitepaper + KMS playbook, and a sample billing model/spreadsheet. Expect those by tomorrow EOD.
[16:20] Maya (Marigold): That timeline works.
[16:26] Sofia (Marigold): One more question about backup and snapshots — do you retain KV caches or session state in backups that might contain PII?
[16:34] Priya (Redwood): We avoid storing PII in caches by default; session states can be configured to be ephemeral. We'll document retention rules and encryption at rest.
[16:47] [20:00] Ravi (Marigold): If we choose Private deployment, how long is the typical lead time for on-prem packaging?
[20:07] Priya (Redwood): For VPC-based private deployments it's 2-4 weeks for initial onboarding; on-prem full HSM-integrated packages vary and can take 6-10 weeks depending on network approvals.
[20:21] Evan (Redwood): We'll note that in the pilot planning doc.
[20:28] Sofia (Marigold): For the pilot, we want one week of warm-up and then two production-like weeks. So total three. Budget team wants a cost cap beforehand.
[20:38] Evan (Redwood): Understood — we'll put a cost estimate and a hard cap line in the pilot sheet.
[20:45] Maya (Marigold): Anything on rights to data derivatives? We need to ensure model outputs aren't claimed as IP by vendor.
[20:54] Evan (Redwood): Our standard MSA states customers retain rights to their data and derived outputs; we'll surface that clause in the DPA/MSA mapping.
[21:03] Priya (Redwood): Last logistics — who'll be our single point of contact on the Marigold side?
[21:10] Sofia (Marigold): Procurement will own contracting, but Ravi will own security checks and Maya will escalate legal redlines.
[21:17] Evan (Redwood): Excellent. We'll set up a follow-up meeting after you review the DPA redlines — propose a technical pilot kickoff the week of Oct 11.
[21:25] [25:00] Sofia (Marigold): Quick clarification — does Redwood offer a data processing addendum template with options toggled for Private vs Hosted?
[25:08] Evan (Redwood): Yes we have template DPA with toggles; we'll produce a marked copy showing differences.
[25:17] Maya (Marigold): We'll need explicit language around audit rights and frequency.
[25:22] Evan (Redwood): Noted.
[25:30] Priya (Redwood): Anything else?
[25:33] Ravi (Marigold): One more — network egress: if we use dedicated pools in region A but Marigold's clients are in region B, can you route to region B to avoid cross-region fees?
[25:45] Priya (Redwood): Yes routing policies can prioritize region-local capacity; we can also mirror caches to reduce cross-region egress.
[25:56] Sofia (Marigold): Great.
[26:00] Evan (Redwood): To recap: we'll send DPA notes, security pack, and billing model; Priya will prepare pilot runbook; Marigold to send sample traffic and security/KMS requirements.
[26:15] Maya (Marigold): Timeline — legal will try to get comments in by Oct 4.
[26:20] Evan (Redwood): Perfect. We'll schedule a 30-minute reconvene the week after to review legal comments.
[26:28] [30:00] Speaker 3: (brief interruption)
[30:12] Priya (Redwood): Closing note — our pilot metrics will include cost per 1k responses, 99/95 pctl latencies, tail latency, error rate, and quality regression alerts.
[30:29] Sofia (Marigold): Thanks. That gives procurement enough to move forward.
[30:36] Evan (Redwood): Thank you all. We'll follow up with links and the action items.
[30:43] Maya (Marigold): Thanks team.
[30:48] Ravi (Marigold): Bye.
[30:52] [End]
